# SEO and GEO audit: acme-mugs This is a small client-side React and Vite single-page app with two routes, `/` and `/catalogue`. I read all six source files. I haven't built or run the app, and there is no live site to check. Problems are ordered by severity. ## Critical (blocks indexing or AI citation) 1. **`public/robots.txt:1-2` blocks all crawlers.** - `User-agent: *` with `Disallow: /` tells Google, Bing and AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and others) not to crawl anything. - Fix: replace the file with: ``` User-agent: * Allow: / Sitemap: https:///sitemap.xml ``` - If it was a staging safeguard, apply the block only to non-production environments. 2. **The site is client-side rendered only, so the initial HTML has no content.** - `index.html:8` ships an empty `
`. All content is rendered by JavaScript from `src/main.jsx:16`. - Many AI crawlers don't execute JS at all, and Google defers rendering. Those crawlers see a blank page. - Fix: pre-render or server-render the routes. Options are SSG/prerendering (for example `vite-plugin-prerender`, or `vite-react-ssg`), or moving to a framework with SSR such as React Router framework mode or Next.js. - Pre-rendering `/` and `/catalogue` is enough for a site this size. 3. **Catalogue content is fetched client-side, at `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:5-7`.** - Products only appear after `fetch('/api/mugs')` resolves in `useEffect`. Even with pre-rendering, the product list would be empty unless the data is loaded at build or server time. - Fix: load the data in a route loader, or in a build-time step, and render it into the HTML. ## High 4. **`index.html:5` has the default title "Vite App" on every page.** - Fix: give each route its own unique title, such as "Handmade Ceramic Mugs | Acme Mugs" for Home and "Mug Catalogue | Acme Mugs" for the catalogue. - Set titles per route with React 19's native ``, or with react-helmet-async. 5. **`index.html:3-6` has no meta description, canonical link, viewport, or `lang`.** - Missing items: - `<html lang="en">` (line 2) - `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` - a per-route `<meta name="description">` - `<link rel="canonical">` - The missing viewport tag also hurts mobile-first indexing. 6. **`src/main.jsx:11` navigates with `<button onClick={() => navigate('/catalogue')}>` instead of a link.** - Crawlers don't click buttons, so they can't find `/catalogue`. Nothing else links to it. Keyboard and screen-reader users also lose link behaviour. - Fix: use `<Link to="/catalogue">Catalogue</Link>`, and remove `useNavigate` from the import on line 2. 7. **There are no structured data (JSON-LD) blocks anywhere.** - Add these to the pre-rendered HTML: - `Organization` (name, logo, location Bristol) on Home. This is the main entity signal for AI engines. - `Product` with `offers` (price, currency, availability) for each mug, and an `ItemList` on the catalogue page. - This is the biggest GEO lever once the site is crawlable. ## Medium 8. **`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:11` renders products as bare `<p>{m.name}</p>`.** - There are no links, no detail pages, and no price, description, or image. - Fix: give each mug its own URL (such as `/catalogue/:slug`) with an `<h2>` and a descriptive paragraph. Link to it from the list with `<Link>`. - Add the detail URLs to the sitemap. Without them there is little for search engines or LLMs to index or quote. 9. **`src/pages/Home.jsx:5` has `<img src="/hero.jpg" />` with no `alt`, dimensions, or loading hints.** - Fix: add `alt="Handmade ceramic mug on a wooden table"` (or whatever the image shows) and `width` and `height` to avoid layout shift (CLS). Use `fetchpriority="high"` because it is the likely LCP image. Consider WebP/AVIF. - `hero.jpg` also isn't in `public/`, so the image will 404 as the repo stands. 10. **`src/pages/Home.jsx:4-6` has thin content.** - There is one sentence of body copy. The "thrown by hand in Bristol, shipped worldwide" claim is the sort of fact AI answers quote, but it needs more support. - Add short sections on materials, glaze, care, shipping and returns, and a few FAQs. Use clear headings and direct answers that can be extracted. - Add an About or contact page with a real address and email for trust (E-E-A-T). 11. **There is no `sitemap.xml`.** - Add `public/sitemap.xml` (or generate it at build time) listing `/`, `/catalogue` and the product pages. Reference it from `robots.txt`. 12. **Social and link-preview tags are missing from `index.html`.** - Add `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:type`, `og:url` and `twitter:card`. - These also feed AI chat link previews. ## Low 13. **`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6` has no error or empty handling.** If `/api/mugs` fails, the fetch rejects unhandled and the user and crawlers see an empty page. Add a `.catch` and a fallback message. 14. **`index.html` has no favicon and no `<meta name="theme-color">`.** 15. **`src/main.jsx` has no 404 route.** Unknown URLs render only the nav. For a static host, add a catch-all `*` route with a real 404 page, and make sure the server returns an HTTP 404 status rather than 200 for unknown paths (soft-404). 16. **No `llms.txt`.** This is optional and its benefit is unproven, but a short `public/llms.txt` summarising the shop and key URLs is cheap. ## Suggested order of work 1. Fix `robots.txt` (a one-minute change). 2. Add pre-rendering, and load the catalogue data at build time. 3. Replace the nav button with a `<Link>`, and add per-route titles, descriptions and canonicals. 4. Add JSON-LD, product detail pages, and the sitemap. 5. Do the image and content improvements. I can make these changes if you'd like. I'd start with items 1, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 11, which don't need an architecture decision. The pre-rendering choice (item 2) is yours to make.
